summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR171 crore with EBITDA margin at 23.6%, but order inflow lagged and management pushed new order wins into Q2 FY27.
summary.overview: Ceinsys Tech reported best-ever quarterly operating revenue of INR171 crore (up 20% YoY), EBITDA of INR40 crore (up 50%, 23.6% margin) and PAT of INR37 crore (up 70%). Full-year FY26 operating revenue was INR661 crore (up 58%), EBITDA INR145 crore (21.9% margin) and PAT INR133 crore (up 111%). Q4 order booking was only INR62 crore, and management said several Q4 closures slipped into Q1 and Q2 FY27. Analysts pressed on order inflow, unbilled revenue (around INR330-350 crore), receivables aging, and the loss-making US subsidiary (VTS), where management guided to breakeven in FY27.

segments.name: Geospatial Engineering Services
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR102 crore (+75% YoY); FY26 INR359 crore (+76%). Largest contributor to growth in the quarter.

segments.name: Technology Solutions
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR68 crore, slightly down YoY; management attributed this to milestone timing, not demand. FY26 INR301 crore (+41%).

segments.name: Mobility and product solutions
segments.commentary: Run-rate businesses outside the order book, together contributing about INR150 crore of annual top line per management.

segments.name: VTS (US subsidiary, telecom geospatial)
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR7-8 crore, EBITDA positive before BD expenses but negative after. Management targets FY27 revenue above INR20 crore (more than 2x), with positive EBITDA and breakeven at subsidiary level.

guidance_outlook: Management expects order inflow in Q2 FY27 to match FY26 order intake (about INR350 crore), and to exceed it by Q2-Q3 FY27; it did not quantify the pipeline.
Three large projects where the company is L1 (transport, energy, infrastructure) and one LOI already under execution but not yet declared as a firm order.
Subsidiaries expected to reach breakeven in FY27, with some BD expense still possible; consolidated EBITDA drag expected to end by year-end.
Unbilled revenue expected to convert to billing substantially in Q1 and Q2 FY27 as government milestones are certified.
Tax rate guided at 25% (including surcharge) from FY27-28, after one-time credits; FY26 lower tax was due to refund and reversal of excess provision.
Government share of business targeted to fall from about 70% to below 50% over 2-3 years, with international growing faster; no numeric growth guidance given.
IP development outlay of INR12-15 crore planned for FY27 across at least 3 IPs, expensed through revenue expenditure.
Proposed change in use of INR235 crore preferential issue proceeds: acquisition and expansion allocation cut from about INR210 crore to include JVs, requiring a special resolution by postal ballot.
Management said the due-diligence-stage acquisition could close within 1-2 quarters.
capex_capacity: INR12 crore of technology spend capitalised; remaining subsidiary technology expenditure (about INR40 crore total) expensed.
IP portfolio: 2 IPs filed, registration expected soon; focus on building more IP products over 1-2 years.
Acquisition pipeline: two earlier opportunities dropped over business-continuity concerns; new target at due-diligence stage.
Team: three senior US hires in business development and execution; COO Rahul to head US delivery. International team said to be adequate for current requirements.
demand_pricing: Q4 order inflow was INR62 crore; management said several Q4 closures slipped due to code-of-conduct restrictions (elections) over the prior 12 months.

Recent wins: MHADA contract INR41 crore (integrated project management and GIS platform); ISRO service order with 3-year subscription renewal; Georgia Land Information System INR21-22 crore; US hybrid power transfer case order INR4 crore.
Jal Jeevan Mission is under 15-20% of the order book per management; new pipeline is focused on infrastructure, roads, metros, transport, energy and defence.
Management said project margins are broadly similar across domains, with no sector-wise drag.
Oil and gas exposure is limited to one US contract; management is exploring digital twin and 3D mapping opportunities.
Tech Mahindra collaboration: POCs done, some US projects won by Tech Mahindra being passed to Ceinsys, initially in telecom.

Management attributed margin gains to delivery capacity, a shift to higher-value solutions, skilling (revenue per employee rising from about INR24 lakh in FY24 to about INR55 lakh), and AI-enabled offerings.

qa_highlights.question: What is happening on the acquisition front and what is the funds plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Two earlier targets were dropped over business-continuity issues; a new target is at due diligence for closure in 1-2 quarters. INR210 crore of the INR235 crore raise was earmarked for acquisition and expansion; the Board proposes adding JVs via postal ballot.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables and recovery from government clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors INR153 crore at 31 Mar 2026: INR94 crore under 90 days, INR127 crore under one year, INR27 crore over one year. Over-one-year balances are tied to pending government funds and sanctions, expected in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade payables and unbilled revenue rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Payables are back-to-back with client receivables and will be paid once debtors are realised. Unbilled revenue reflects government milestones not certified by 31 Mar 2026; management expects billing in Q1 and Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Status and outlook of VTS (US subsidiary)?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 turnover about INR7-8 crore, EBITDA positive before BD spend. FY27 target above INR20 crore with positive EBITDA; Q1 is in line with projection.

qa_highlights.question: Order book execution period and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Projects carry 12-18 month execution; spillover expected into the next 2-3 quarters. Management would not give pipeline quantum but said Q1 and Q2 closures should match or exceed the prior year.

qa_highlights.question: Order inflow and bid pipeline versus FY25 and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 inflow would match FY26 intake (about INR350 crore) and exceed it by Q2 or early Q3. Three L1 projects, one LOI under execution. Analyst noted the INR800-plus crore figure referenced was revenue, not order book.

qa_highlights.question: Why is unbilled revenue high and is the accounting aggressive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it follows Ind AS and billing depends on government milestone certification, with about 10 major and 50 small projects on different milestone schedules.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate and FY26 decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower FY26 tax came from an INR8-9 crore refund and reversal of excess FY25 provision. Steady-state tax rate guided at 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the technology solutions decline temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it temporary, citing a missed milestone in Q4; Technology Solutions grew 41% for FY26 and is over 55-60% of contract mix.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy for the next 3-5 years and international mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Government share to fall from about 70% to below 50% over 2-3 years, growing international faster. No numeric growth target given.

risks_watch: Order inflow: Q4 FY26 bookings of INR62 crore; management guidance for Q2 FY27 recovery has already slipped once from Q1.
Unbilled revenue (about INR330-350 crore per analyst) and receivables over one year (INR27 crore) depend on government milestone certification and fund release.
Working capital: payables tied to back-to-back contracts; net working capital cycle still 157 days.
US subsidiary VTS and the wider international business must reach breakeven in FY27 as guided; drag on consolidated margins.
Proposed INR235 crore fund reallocation (JV addition) needs shareholder approval by postal ballot; acquisition not yet closed.
Management team changes: Suraj left, US leadership reorganised, COO Rahul taking over US delivery.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, cash and long-term direction, but cautious and sometimes vague on near-term order timing: several Q4 closures slipped, and management gave no numeric growth or pipeline quantum when pressed.
key_quotes: We have delivered a best-ever quarterly performance, marking continued sequential improvement and extending our growth momentum over the last 8 quarters.
Unfortunately, Q4, we couldn't have these closures. But Q1 and Q2, we have substantial order book to be closed.
We will be able to match what FY 26 will close by Q2. And then we'll be able to surpass what we achieved in FY 26 by Q3.
We will be in breakeven in this financial year. We are targeting to have that breakeven in these subsidiaries, but we may also incur certain expenses towards BD in this financial year also.
So there is no aggressive kind of accounting what we are doing. It is the normal as per Ind AS accounting is being done.
We don't commit any numbers on growth. We keep on pushing ourselves.

growth.why: No numeric company-wide revenue guidance; management expects order inflow to match FY26 (~INR350 crore) by Q2 FY27 and surpass it by Q3, backed by three L1 projects and one LOI not yet firm, plus a VTS target of >INR20 crore revenue in FY27 (vs INR7-8 crore FY26), with recent wins such as the INR41 crore MHADA contract and unbilled revenue of about INR330-350 crore expected to convert in Q1-Q2 FY2
